claims.statement: Every business Bundle roots its code at cn.shopex.ecshopx.<domain> and follows a standard package skeleton: api/admin/v1 and api/front/v1 (+ api/open for callbacks) controllers, service, domain entities, mapper interfaces, dispatch job handlers and event listeners, cron Schedule*Handler classes, port interfaces the Bundle owns, integration implementations of other Bundles' Ports, config, and an optional repository layer; orders, goods, members, and kaquan all follow it, though not every Bundle carries every package (kaquan has no repository/, members has no cron/, goods' cron/ holds only the test-cron mock config).

Controllers are split by API surface: api/admin/v1 controllers carry @AdminAuth (plus @ShopLog) and map /api/v1 or /api/v1/<domain>; api/front/v1 controllers carry @FrontAuth or @FrontNoAuth and always map under /api/v1/h5app, with Mini Program endpoints further namespaced by wxapp; api/open holds unauthenticated callbacks and legacy PHP-URL-compatibility routes such as the WeChat Pay notify endpoint at /wechatAuth/wxpay/notify. The public Open API is served by the dedicated ecshopx-openapi module at /api/openapi/internal/v1|v2 plus a catch-all gateway at /api/openapi, not from business-Bundle api/ packages.

Every controller passes an explicit bean name to @RestController to avoid collisions in the single Spring context that scans cn.shopex.ecshopx.**: the dominant pattern is <domain><Surface>V1<Entity> (ordersAdminV1Order, ordersFrontV1WxappPayment, goodsAdminV1Items, membersFrontV1Members) while kaquan uses the variant <domain><Entity><Surface>V1 (kaquanVipGradeAdminV1, kaquanDiscountCardFrontV1), and the openapi module uses openapiV1*/openapiV2* names.

Mapper bean-name collisions across Bundles are prevented not by manual names but by FqcnMapperBeanNameGenerator, installed by EcshopxApplication via @MapperScan(basePackages = cn.shopex.ecshopx.**.mapper, nameGenerator = FqcnMapperBeanNameGenerator.class, sqlSessionFactoryRef = sqlSessionFactory, lazyInitialization = true); a mapper interface only works if it lives in a mapper package, and its XML only loads via mybatis-plus.mapper-locations=classpath*:mapper/**/*.xml in the bootstrap application.properties.

Write-side service logic in mature Bundles follows a responsibility split: a @Service RequestGate (e.g. DistributorCreateRequestGate) re-reads the operator JWT, enforces menu-permission route aliases, asserts company activation, and narrows entity scope, throwing Unauthorized/BadRequest/Forbidden before business code runs; a stateless ParamValidator with static validate(Map) checks field shape; and an Orchestrator (DistributorCreateOrchestrator) owns @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class), sequences duplicate checks, third-party guard clients, the delegated insert, and registers a TransactionSynchronization whose afterCommit publishes the dispatch job and event in fixed order.

port/ holds interfaces this Bundle owns that other Bundles implement (e.g. orders/port/WxappCartAddPort, whose Javadoc states it is implemented by the goods module to avoid an orders-to-goods dependency, with the implementation at goods/service/cart/wxapp/WxappCartAddPortImpl injected by orders' CartController), while integration/ holds this Bundle's implementations of Ports owned by other Bundles; most shared Port interfaces live in ecshopx-common under common/port/<domain>/ so consumers never depend on providers, which keeps the peer graph acyclic — goods depends on orders and on promotions (the latter so its search promotion-sync listener can read the seckill/group-buy rel-goods mappers), never the reverse, with the promotion→search edge itself inverted through common/port/goods/GoodsSearchIndexDirtyByItemIdsPort.

orders/integration/JushuitanSettingReadPortImpl implements common/port/order/JushuitanSettingReadPort by delegating to the orders-local OrdersErpSettingRedisReadService, letting aftersales and system-link consume the same Port without depending on ecshopx-orders; likewise each Bundle's openapi/ package (e.g. orders/openapi/OpenapiOrderListPortImpl implementing common/openapi/OpenapiOrderListPort) adapts the Bundle to the ecshopx-openapi gateway, which itself depends only on ecshopx-common.

dispatch/ beans come in two shapes implementing interfaces from ecshopx-common: *JobHandler implements DispatchHandler with handle(Map) (e.g. FinishOrderJobHandler normalizing null payload to Map.of() and delegating to FinishOrderJobService) and *DispatchListener implements DispatchListener with onEvent(Map) (e.g. UpdateItemSalesDispatchListener on EVENT_TRADE_FINISH); they are never registered by annotation — ecshopx-bootstrap contains explicit *RegistrationConfig @Configuration classes that call dispatchRegistry.registerJob/registerEventListener in @PostConstruct, and DispatchBusConfig instantiates the DispatchRegistry, DispatchFacade, and the sync/Redis drivers.

Publisher-side dispatch interfaces (FinishOrderJobDispatchPublisher, OrdersTradeFinishDispatchPublisher, DistributionAddEventDispatchPublisher, …) live in ecshopx-common so a Bundle can publish without depending on the bus implementation or the consumer; their DispatchFacade-backed implementations are provided by ecshopx-bootstrap (e.g. FinishOrderJobDispatchPublisherImpl dispatches with ASYNC/REDIS/slow options), and after-commit semantics are provided either inline via TransactionSynchronizationManager in the orchestrator or via a dedicated *AfterCommitDispatchPublisher wrapper bean registered @Primary in the bootstrap.

cron/ holds XXL-JOB handlers named Schedule*Handler that are pure delegators: a @Component with a @XxlJob(short-name) method that times the call, logs done/failed in the [cron][<name>] shape with cost in ms, delegates to a service, and on exception publishes a CronAlertEvent via ApplicationEventPublisher and rethrows so XXL-JOB marks the run failed; orders has 18 such handlers and kaquan's ScheduleCancelExpiredCardHandler follows the same pattern, and the contract is pinned by per-handler tests asserting the log shape and the alert-and-rethrow behaviour.

Every business Bundle's POM depends on ecshopx-common (most add ecshopx-dispatch) plus a curated set of peer Bundles it actually needs; ecshopx-orders lists work-wechat, third-party, supplier, reservation, espier, members, companys, point, aftersales, payment, chinaums-pay, deposit, hfpay, popularize, and super-admin, while ecshopx-bootstrap depends on every Bundle, is the only module with the spring-boot-maven-plugin (mainClass cn.shopex.ecshopx.EcshopxApplication), and carries the Flyway migrations, the global application.properties, and the dispatch-bus and registration configuration.

domain/ entities are annotated with the extended MyBatis-Plus metadata annotations @MpTable/@MpId/@MpField/@MpIndex from common/mybatis/metadata, which are meta-annotated with the stock @TableName/@TableId/@TableField and additionally carry column type, length, nullability, comments, and indexes migrated from the legacy Doctrine ORM; the bin/make-migration helper diffs the live MySQL schema against these domains to generate Flyway SQL under ecshopx-bootstrap/src/main/resources/db/migration, and the readme requires manually reviewing the generated SQL for types, defaults, NULL allowance, comments, and indexes.

repository/ is an optional @Repository layer composing mapper calls into named operations (orders/repository/CategoryTaxRateRepository wraps CategoryTaxRateMapper with findDuplicateForCreate, insertEntity, updateByIdPartialReturningRow owning the MyBatis-Plus wrapper logic); simple flows may call the mappers directly, as FinishOrderBatchService does with NormalOrdersMapper.

Bundle-scoped @RestControllerAdvice classes are tightly scoped to one API surface rather than global: orders/config/OrdersAdminV1ExceptionAdvice uses basePackages = cn.shopex.ecshopx.orders.api.admin.v1 and maps BadRequest/Resource exceptions to a Dingo-style 200-with-data envelope, while kaquan's DiscountCardControllerExceptionAdvice lives next to the controllers in api/admin/v1 and scopes by assignableTypes; both are ordered @Order(HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE).

event/ and listener/ form a lighter third async mechanism distinct from the dispatch bus and cron: plain Spring ApplicationEvents (PaySuccessSpringEvent, NormalOrderCancelSpringEvent, OrderProcessLogSpringEvent) consumed by @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT, fallbackExecution = true) beans such as orders/listener/OrderProcessLogSpringEventListener, used for intra-Bundle after-commit work that does not need retry or cross-Bundle fan-out.

config/ holds Bundle-local Spring beans (e.g. orders/config/OrdersSchedulingConfig with @EnableScheduling, executor configs, and the scoped advice classes), and the cron/testcfg/CronTestMockConfig class in src/main (not src/test) is annotated @Profile(test-cron) to swap side-effect beans such as dispatch publishers, Redis writes, and third-party ports for No-op implementations during cron-diff testing.

When a Port implementation would otherwise create a dependency cycle, ecshopx-bootstrap supplies the adapter itself: e.g. bootstrap/order/CompanyPassportUidByCompanyIdPortAdapter implements common/port/companys/CompanyPassportUidByCompanyIdPort by delegating to CompanysMapper, sitting alongside the bootstrap's many cn.shopex.ecshopx.config.*RegistrationConfig and *DispatchPublisherImpl classes that wire cross-Bundle jobs and events.

api/pos/v1 is a fourth controller surface for POS terminals: controllers carry neither @AdminAuth nor @FrontAuth and instead rely on a POS JWT Bearer token verified upstream by espier/security/PosJwtAuthenticationFilter, which engages only for tokens with token_kind=pos (issuer POS_JWT_ISSUER, default ecshopx-pos) and populates the PosJwtRequestAttributes.POS_JWT_USER_DATA request attribute; companys/api/pos/v1/PosAuthController (bean name companysPosV1PosAuth, mapping /api/v1/pos/auth) exposes login (employee number + password), logout (blacklists the presented token via PosJwtIssuerPort.invalidate), and me (claims read from the request attribute).

api/callback/v1 holds vendor-signed callbacks that cannot use admin/front/POS auth: shuyun's ShuyunOpenPlatformTokenCallbackController, ShuyunOpenPlatformLoyaltyGradeCallbackController, and ShuyunOfflineBenefitCallbackController read the raw request body (the signature covers exact bytes), delegate verification to the Bundle's auth/ package, and return the vendor's expected response shape ({code,msg,data} for Shuyun) rather than the ApiResult envelope.

shuyun/auth/InboundSignedCallbackPreparer is the reference inbound-verification layer: prepare(request, rawBody, mode) resolves the tenant by appId (query first, then body) with platCode/shadow-benefitId fallbacks, verifies the callback HMAC via CallbackSignatureVerifier using the configured callbackIdentitySecret from ShuyunOpenPlatformProperties (prefix ecshopx.shuyun.open-platform, distinct from per-tenant DB app_secret), then enforces freshness/once-only via InboundSignedCallbackReplayGuard (Redis keys with configurable skew/TTL) — only after a valid signature — with the InboundSignedPrepareMode enum (TOKEN/LOYALTY_MEMBER_GRADE_CHANGE/OFFLINE_BENEFIT) selecting the per-endpoint error-body dialect, returning InboundPrepareResult.Ok(companyId, body) or Err(ResponseEntity).

POS credential logic lives in companys/service/posauth: PosAuthService.login re-reads the PosStoreAccount row, decrypts the password cipher via common/crypto/SensitiveFieldEncryptor, rejects disabled/resigned accounts and accounts whose shop is_valid is closed/delete (enabled/disabled and legacy 1/0 allowed), builds a claim map with token_kind=pos and employee_id aliased to the employee number, and delegates token issuance to common/auth/PosJwtIssuerPort — implemented by espier/security/PosJwtIssuer (HS512, TTL from JWT_TTL) with logout blacklisting via common/auth/PosJwtBlacklistPort; PosJwtSessionValidator implements common/auth/PosJwtSessionValidatorPort so the espier filter can invalidate stale sessions, meaning the credential-table owner makes the login decision while JWT mechanics stay behind common/auth Ports in the security Bundle.

Bundles owning a vendor integration keep one outbound HTTP client in client/ or gateway/: digios/client/DigiOsGatewayClient builds its own RestTemplate (5s connect/30s read, package-private ctor for test mocks), resolves per-company config via DigiOsConfigService (ecshopx.digios.* properties overlaid by the DigiOsCompanyConfig DB row), fetches a Redis-cached token from DigiOsTokenService, signs calls with X-Auth-Client/X-Auth-Token/X-Message-Id, logs every attempt including 4xx/5xx to the digios_api_log table, retries exactly once on token-unauthorized after clearing the token cache, and returns a failed result instead of throwing when the integration is disabled or config incomplete; shuyun/gateway/ShuyunOpenGatewayClient plays the same role for the Shuyun open-api.

Optional cross-Bundle Ports use a NoOp default plus a @Primary override: common/port/digios/PosStoreAccountDigiOsCreatePortNoOp is a @Component no-op so the consumer (companys' PosStoreAccountWriteService.create, which calls ensureSyncedOnCreate before inserting the local row) always has a bean, while digios/port/PosStoreAccountDigiOsCreatePortImpl is the @Primary real implementation that upserts the DigiOS account and throws BadRequestException on failure to block the local create — so the consumer Bundle needs no Maven dependency on the provider Bundle.

Dispatch listeners may live in a different Bundle than the event owner and outside the Bundle's dispatch/ package: all five digios/dispatch/*DispatchListener classes react to events owned by distribution, orders/aftersales, and companys (distributor create/update, order-delivery store adjustment, aftersales return adjustment, operator create), each bound by its own ecshopx-bootstrap *RegistrationConfig (e.g. DigiOsDistributorCreateDispatchListenerRegistrationConfig registers DistributionDispatchEventNames.EVENT_DISTRIBUTOR_CREATE with ListenerDispatchOptions.async at @Order(79)), shuyun/dispatch carries twelve listeners of the same shape, and goods keeps its stock-change listener inside its search feature package (search/sync/ItemStoreUpdatedSearchIndexDispatchListener on GoodsDispatchEventNames.EVENT_ITEM_STORE_UPDATE, registered sync at @Order(76)); publisher implementations for such events also live in the bootstrap (DigiOsAftersalesReturnAdjustmentDispatchPublisherImpl publishes via DispatchFacade with ASYNC/REDIS/platform-default retry).

ecshopx-digios is the reference recipe for wiring a new Bundle without peer dependencies on its consumers: its POM declares only ecshopx-common plus ecshopx-goods and ecshopx-distribution (no companys/orders/aftersales/espier and no ecshopx-dispatch), inbound sync triggers arrive via dispatch listeners registered by bootstrap configs, synchronous hooks go through common Ports with NoOp defaults, outbound capability is exposed via common/openapi (OpenapiDigiOsProductStockPushPortImpl implementing OpenapiDigiOsProductStockPushPort for the openapi gateway), and assembly happens only in ecshopx-bootstrap/pom.xml which lists every Bundle including ecshopx-digios and ecshopx-shuyun.

A Bundle that owns a full-text search engine keeps the subsystem in one top-level search/ package: goods/search/ roots the feature flag and client wiring (SearchEsProperties on prefix ecshopx.search.es with enabled default false, likeFallback, hosts, alias, and timeouts; SearchEsClientConfig builds a dedicated ElasticsearchClient from elasticsearch-java 8.15.5 declared only in the goods POM) and subdivides into query/ (GoodsSearchQuery/GoodsSearchEsQueryBuilder/GoodsSearchQueryService), index/ (MybatisSearchIndexSourceLoader, SearchIndexMapper, GoodsSearchMappingService, GoodsSearchIndexRepository keyed by GoodsSearchDocumentId(companyId, distributorId, defaultItemId)), sync/ (incremental dirty-mark pipeline), rebuild/ (full reindex as a dispatch job), synonym/ (synonym sets with hot reload whose cross-Bundle edge is SearchSynonymImportFinishPortImpl implementing common/espier/upload/SearchSynonymImportFinishPort for the espier upload machinery), and price/ (member-tier and effective-price calculation for ES sort/filter).

Incremental search-index freshness in goods is a three-piece after-commit pipeline: GoodsSearchIndexDirtyFanout converts one logical change into one dirty mark per distributor (headquarters distributor_id=0 plus every distinct distributor carrying the default item from DistributorItemsRepository, per-distributor scheduling failures only WARNed); SearchIndexSyncScheduler turns each mark into a GoodsSearchDirtyEvent published after commit via TransactionSynchronization when a transaction is active (immediately otherwise); and SearchIndexSyncListeners (@TransactionalEventListener AFTER_COMMIT with fallbackExecution) hands the event to SearchIndexUpdater, which no-ops when ES is disabled and otherwise upserts or deletes the single document with up to 3 attempts, logging instead of throwing on exhaustion.

The storefront goods list read path switches between DB and ES per request: when ecshopx.search.es.enabled is off (or the salesman gate short-circuits) WxappGoodsItemsListServiceImpl stays on WxappGoodsItemsListQueryOrchestrator.queryItemListData; when on it delegates to GoodsSearchFacade.queryListWithHydration, which searches ES for ordered default_item_ids, hydrates those ids through the same DB orchestrator with an internal single-page override (page 1, size capped at 50, accept-language passthrough), re-orders rows into ES order, writes the ES sale price into the row price in fen while keeping effectivePriceFen strictly for sort/filter, corrects total_count by the number of documents DB hydration dropped, and on GoodsSearchEsException either falls back to the DB path (likeFallback, which keeps the keyword LIKE pre-resolve the param builder otherwise skips) or logs and returns an empty list.

common/port/goods/GoodsSearchIndexDirtyByItemIdsPort lets promotion write paths dirty the search index without depending on goods: it exposes SKU-level scheduleUpsertForItemIds(companyId, itemIds) with a @ConditionalOnMissingBean NoOp default in common, and the sole implementation goods/integration/GoodsSearchIndexDirtyByItemIdsPortImpl resolves each SKU item_id to its default_item_id via ItemsRepository and DefaultItemIdResolver (passing unresolved ids through unchanged) before delegating to the dirty fanout; the observed caller is goods' own search/sync/GoodsSearchIndexPromotionSyncListener, which reacts to SeckillActivityCommittedEvent, SeckillActivityEndCommittedEvent, and PromotionGroupActivityCommittedEvent, resolving rel-goods rows through the promotions mappers (allowed because ecshopx-goods depends on ecshopx-promotions, never the reverse) and calling the Port rather than the fanout directly.

Full search reindex is exposed as a dispatch-bus job: goods/search/rebuild/SearchRebuildJobHandler implements DispatchHandler under common GoodsSearchDispatchJobNames.SEARCH_REBUILD_JOB (job:198:GoodsBundle\Jobs\SearchRebuildJob) with payloads for all-active-companies rebuild, per-company upsert into the current alias, or single-company blue-green; SearchRebuildService implements blue-green as new physical index, bulk indexing in batches of 500, then alias switch; the producer side follows the standard pattern with the SearchRebuildJobDispatchPublisher interface in ecshopx-common, a bootstrap SearchRebuildJobDispatchPublisherImpl dispatching ASYNC/REDIS on the slow queue with platform-default retry, and SearchRebuildJobRegistrationConfig binding the handler in the registry.

Goods write orchestrators act as feature-integration seams: ItemsCreateOrchestrator.createItemsReturningItemId branches on supplier_id (supplier creates delegate entirely to SupplierItemsAddService and return 0; platform creates run PlatformItemsAddService.addItemsTransactional, then DistributorGoodsSyncService.syncGoods, then GoodsSearchIndexDirtyFanout.scheduleUpsertForDefaultItem in fixed order), and ItemsUpdateOrchestrator repeats the same three-step tail for the platform-update branch while routing supplier audit states through SupplierItemsReviewGoodsService, so the transactional write services below stay unaware of distributor sync and the search index.
